epics.title: Routing modes: standard, custom tiers, dynamic switch

links.reason: resolves models for ask/chat/research
records the resolved model

epics.description: Three consumer modes set by config. Standard (default): one model, default perplexity/sonar (probed live 2026-10-13: web search works, about $0.0038 per call; 'auto' is rejected by the API). Custom: user's light/standard/complex model tiers, validated against the live catalog; caller picks the tier via depth. Dynamic: opt-in, classifier picks the tier (see routing-decisions-classifier). Open design problem: how the calling agent learns the active mode (server instructions rendered from settings, resolved mode/tier/model in every result, active routing in perplexity_models). README setup section lays out the three choices.

epics.title: Image, audio and file inputs on ask and chat, with modality-aware routing

links.reason: the router must pick a model that accepts the attached media

epics.description: perplexity_ask and perplexity_chat take text only, so a user cannot hand Perplexity an image, audio clip or document. An MCP server's callers are unknown; someone will ask to send an image and do something with it. Add attachment parameters (shape probed from the live Agent API first), validate size and type locally, record cost, and give the router (routing-v2) a modality requirement so it only considers models whose probed input modalities include it. Our omission, found 2026-10-15 while designing routing-v2.

epics.title: Router v2: pick a model and an effort level per prompt from benchmark evidence and price

links.reason: needs the matrix of models, prices and accepted efforts
the evaluation is the gate for the shortlist and for publishing
modality requirement

epics.description: Replace the three-tier effort ladder with a choice of (model, effort) in ask, chat and research. Candidates are a curated shortlist backed by published benchmark data (Perplexity Research per provider family, cited) and our own evaluation; among models within a few points on the relevant benchmark the cheaper wins. Effort not accepted by the model is dropped. Fallbacks: model gpt-6-luna, effort low. Research may use high and xhigh (background); ask and chat cap effort to what fits 120 s. Explicit model/depth/tier still win. Not published until an evaluation shows it picks well.

notes.text: lane: openspec, as routed. Presets are bundles (docs: fast = 1 web search, low = 1 search + 1 fetch, medium = 2+2, high = 3+3); a router on an explicit model must attach comparable tools or it answers with weaker grounding than preset medium.

2026-10-29 inputs: effort levels now fast, low, medium, high, xhigh and ultra-preview (docs/research/2026-10-29-api-drift); high runs gpt-6.1-terra; the matrix auto-added gpt-6.1-terra and marked nemotron-3-ultra removed; Decisions flash model costs half. Rob decided on 2026-10-29: do not release the matrix or dynamic routing (2.1.0 and 2.2.0 are not published); routing-v2 will replace them and the next release comes when the router is confirmed sustainable.
